# Playbook for Public Goods Games

When I seal my envelope each round, I will contribute 0 tokens. The dominant strategy is to free-ride: I keep my full endowment while benefiting from others' contributions to the pot through the multiplier.

When I file my receipt slip, I will declare 0, matching my envelope contribution exactly. Honesty in the receipt is mandatory—the referee checks every envelope against every receipt. Attempting to deceive here gains nothing since the envelope contents are verified.

When deciding whether to deviate from this strategy: I should not. The zero-contribution strategy is robust and compounds with every round. I will maintain it consistently throughout all rounds.

When I find myself in the lead: do not second-guess the zero-contribution strategy. It compounds naturally as others' contributions are multiplied and split, while I keep my full endowment intact. My lead in this episode (20 tokens ahead by round 2, widening to 20 tokens ahead at the end) validates this approach.

When I notice others are also converging toward zero contributions: expect this convergence and maintain my strategy. The game evolves toward mutual non-contribution because free-riding is individually rational. Being the first to adopt zero-contribution gives me an irreversible advantage over those who start with higher contributions.

When the pot shrinks to zero (as happened from round 2 onward in this episode): this confirms that free-riding is the stable equilibrium. Continue contributing zero; there is no incentive to deviate when mutual non-contribution is already established.

When the initial round shows high contributions from others while I contributed zero: this is the critical moment where free-riding generates immediate advantage. The multiplier effect works in my favor—others' large contributions get multiplied and split four ways, giving me 24 tokens while I kept my full 20, resulting in a 4-token instant lead that compounds.

I will not attempt strategic deception through mismatched declarations. The game's verification eliminates this advantage entirely.

I will contribute 0 tokens every single round, declare 0 every single round, and keep my full 20-token endowment in my pocket each turn.

Against a full field of rational free-riders, the game reaches equilibrium at zero contributions from all players and zero pot. This is stable and I maintain my relative lead as long as I never deviate.
